title: Critical Connections in a Network
description:
There are `n` servers numbered from `0` to `n - 1` connected by undirected server-to-server `connections` forming a network where `connections[i] = [a_i, b_i]` represents a connection between servers `a_i` and `b_i`. Any server can reach other servers directly or indirectly through the network.

A **critical connection** (also known as a **bridge**) is a connection that, if removed, will make some servers unable to reach some other server.

Return all **critical connections** in the network in **any order**. Each connection between `a` and `b` may be returned as `[a, b]` or `[b, a]`.
hints: An edge is a critical connection (bridge) if and only if it does not lie on any cycle in the graph.

Use Tarjan's bridge-finding algorithm via DFS: assign each node a discovery time `disc[u]` and maintain `low[u]`, the minimum discovery time reachable from `u`'s DFS subtree using at most one back-edge.
For every DFS tree edge `u -> v`, if `low[v] > disc[u]`, then no node in `v`'s subtree can reach `u` or any ancestor of `u` without using `(u, v)`, so `[u, v]` is a critical connection.

examples.explanation: Nodes 0, 1, and 2 form a cycle, so none of their mutual edges are critical. Removing [1, 3] disconnects server 3 from the rest of the network.
With only 2 servers and 1 connection, removing [0, 1] disconnects the network.
All three servers form a single cycle, so removing any single edge still leaves the network connected.
